subject: EU residency: evaluation charter, stakeholder roles & MAP milestones
messages:
From: Sabrina Klein <sabrina.k@eucorp.com>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Jens Müller <jens.mueller@datarules.de>, Legal Team <legal@eucorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency alignment — can we run a MAP + evaluation cadence?

Hi Rohaan (and team),

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, the execs want a formal mutual action plan that captures acceptance criteria for a limited MVP (data residency and cross-border safeguards), the evaluation cadence, and the signoffs required to reach a POC close in Q1.

Key asks from our side:
- Clear roles (who is our technical contact, DPO reviewer, procurement contact)
- A short evaluation charter with pass/fail criteria for residency (where data is stored, in-transit controls, access controls)
- A proposed timeline with milestone dates and gating decisions

Can Redwood propose a one-pager MAP + evaluation charter we can review? We’d like to run a joint kickoff next week and lock a final timeline by Thanksgiving week.

Attaching a small vendor questionnaire that procurement likes to use (we'll share answers after the kickoff).

Thanks,
Sabrina
VP Product Operations
EUCorp GmbH

Attachment: EUCorp_vendor_questionnaire.docx (stub)

From: rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Klein <sabrina.k@eucorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jens Müller <jens.mueller@datarules.de>, Legal Team <legal@eucorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency alignment — can we run a MAP + evaluation cadence?

Hi Sabrina — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks.

I’m looping in Laura (Customer Success lead for EU accounts) and Marissa (Solutions) so we can build a concise MAP and an evaluation charter that maps to your procurement checkpoints. I attached two documents: a short Evaluation Charter (draft) and a proposed MAP timeline spreadsheet with milestone dates.

Topline proposal (draft):
- MAP scope: residency (EU regional data-at-rest), cross-border export policy (SCCs + encryption-at-rest), and restricted support access (KMS controls).
- MVP acceptance: data stored in eu-central-1 only for production; test/staging can use eu-west-1 with documented scope; successful data export test demonstrating SCCs + encryption; DPO signoff on data flows.
- Evaluation cadence: 2-week sprint cycles for integration work, with formal checkpoints on Day 14 (ingest test) and Day 35 (export/security validation).

Please review the attached Evaluation_Charter_v1 and eu-map-timeline and call out anything missing. Proposed kickoff: 2026-11-24 14:00 CET (I’ll send a calendar invite once we confirm attendees).

Next actions I propose:
1) Sabrina: confirm DPO/Legal reviewer and procurement contact (name + email).
2) Jens: can you confirm if the on-prem connector we discussed supports pseudonymization at ingest?
3) Laura/Marissa: will draft acceptance test templates and owner mapping.

Best,
Rohaan Mehta
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: evaluation_charter_v1.pdf; eu-map-timeline.xlsx

Date: 2026-11-21T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency alignment — can we run a MAP + evaluation cadence?

Hi all — adding a little more structure from the CS side so we can speed review.

Stakeholder matrix (proposed):
- Executive sponsor: Sabrina Klein (EUCorp)
- Procurement lead: (Sabrina — please confirm)
- DPO reviewer: EUCorp DPO 
- Technical lead: Jens Müller (EUCorp) / Redwood solutions (Marissa)
- Integration owner (Redwood): Laura Bennett

MVP acceptance criteria (short):
1) Data-at-rest proof: evidence that production datasets are stored exclusively in eu-central-1 for the POC timeframe (logs + console screenshots).
2) Cross-border control: demonstration of SCCs in outbound flows and TLS + envelope encryption between regions.
3) Access controls: role-based access screenshot + audit link showing restricted support access and key separation.
4) Performance check: 95th percentile latency within agreed bounds for the test workload (we can define the workload in the checklist).

I also added suggested owners in the Evaluation_Charter_v1 (attached). I'll draft the acceptance-test checklist and share before the kickoff.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency alignment — can we run a MAP + evaluation cadence?

Hi — Hannah from Product Ops here. Quick notes ahead of the kickoff:

1) Timeline tweaks: to get legal signoff we should plan a parallel review thread for the DPA and SCCs. I updated the eu-map-timeline.xlsx to include a legal review window (Day 7–14) and a final gating decision on Day 42.
2) Technical note: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and we’ll document key separation for support access in the Evaluation_Charter_v1.
3) Risk ask: Sabrina — will your team require on-prem air-gapped demos or is a VPC deployment sufficient for initial evaluation? That determines whether we run the export verification in your environment or ours.

I attached an initial MAP template that includes the sprint-by-sprint evaluation checklist and acceptance test templates. Please review and flag if we should include SOC 2 artifact requests in the first pass.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
